newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Three strikes law jails Australian boy for year.
newsitem.headline: Three strikes law jails Australian boy for year.

text.p: A 12-year-old Australian boy has been jailed for a year after stealing three bicycles, an ice cream and A$5 (US$3.85) under a controversial law that automatically jails a person after a third conviction.
The Australian Council for Civil Liberties on Saturday called for the "three strikes" law in Western Australia state, the only one in the country, to be overturned.
Council spokesman Terry O'Gorman warned that society would eventually suffer a violent backlash from young offenders jailed under the law.

"While it might make the law and order 'tub thumpers' feel self-satisfied, they are in fact creating a situation where more and more of these youths are put away, when judges say they shouldn't, and society will bear the brunt of their increased anger and increased offending," O'Gorman told reporters.

The unnamed Aboriginal boy was sentenced to 12 months detention by the Perth Children's Court on Friday after being convicted of a third home burglary. The boy had acted as a look-out and received three stolen bicycles, an ice cream and A$5 from the latest robbery.
The sentencing judge also criticised the "three strikes" law.
"The community should be able to find another way of dealing with a person like you than locking you up in a city institution," said judge Allan Fenbury.
Under the law, which came into force last November, any person, adult or juvenile, faces a mandatory sentence of at least 12 months jail if convicted for a third time.
